market_outlook: This is a company-specific earnings note with no broad directional market commentary from Adam. No macro or Fed context is provided in this edition.

company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS estimates ($56.05 vs. $54.03 Street) but the quality was low — 145 basis points of gross margin tailwind came from tariff refunds and another 105 basis points from a non-cash LIFO benefit. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. the +3.1% expected, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal expands Cognex's footprint into the rapidly growing physical AI and robotics space.

MillerKnoll delivered a solid FQ1 EPS beat (53 cents vs. 36 cents Street), and notably would have beaten even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind (42 cents adjusted vs. 36 cents expected). Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. the $943.2 million consensus, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Full-year fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88–$4.03 billion from $3.93–$4.13 billion, while EPS guidance was left unchanged at $1.85–$2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1st, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings prior CFO experience at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a leadership change with no financial results attached.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS estimates (78 cents vs. 87 cents Street) as gross margins collapsed 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the 13.85% expected, and management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, inflation, and rising material costs as headwinds. Revenue of $2.311 billion was actually slightly above the $2.17 billion estimate but couldn't offset the margin damage. Bright spots include healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost actions underway, and a backlog surge of roughly 75% year-over-year in North American towable RVs, though North American motorized RV backlog fell ~28%.

Viking Therapeutics shares surged in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. This is a significant clinical readout that reinforces the drug's competitive positioning in the highly watched obesity/GLP-1 space. The result is a clear positive catalyst for the stock.

sectors: RV industry facing macro headwinds per THOR management — stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure on household budgets keeping retail soft. GLP-1/obesity drug space sees another positive data point with VKTX's VK2735 trial results. Robotics and physical AI getting a deal-driven spotlight via Cognex's RealSense acquisition.
tts_summary:
Good morning. Today's note is a pure earnings and company news edition — no broad macro commentary, no Fed color, just a tight set of pre-market catalysts to work through heading into Tuesday's open.

Let's start with the most exciting one. Viking Therapeutics is spiking in pre-market after reporting positive trial results for its GLP-1 weight loss drug VK2735, showing twenty-two percent weight loss in participants. That's a major clinical win and puts Viking firmly in the conversation as a credible competitor in the obesity drug race. Watch for sympathy moves across the GLP-1 complex.

AutoZone beat on fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share — fifty-six oh five versus the fifty-four oh three the Street was looking for — but the quality of that beat is questionable. Two hundred and fifty basis points of gross margin help came from tariff refunds and a non-cash LIFO adjustment. Strip those out and the picture looks worse. Domestic comps missed at plus one point six percent versus plus three point one percent expected, and operating expenses as a percent of sales ticked up one hundred basis points year-over-year. Management says linearity improved in the back half of the quarter and they feel well positioned for fiscal twenty-seven, but the headline beat is going to get picked apart.

Cognex is making a move into physical AI and robotics perception, acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras — for roughly five hundred million upfront plus about one hundred and six and a half million more. RealSense is expected to generate eighty to ninety million in revenue, growing more than fifty percent year-over-year. This is a strategic bet on the robotics build-out cycle and positions Cognex for a space with significant long-term tailwinds.

MillerKnoll delivered a clean earnings beat — fifty-three cents versus thirty-six cents expected — and importantly, even backing out an eleven-cent tariff refund tailwind, they still beat at forty-two cents. Sales missed and full-year revenue guidance was trimmed modestly, but EPS guidance held steady. Mixed, but the quality of the earnings beat stands out positively.

THOR Industries is the weak link this morning. The RV maker missed fiscal fourth quarter earnings per share — seventy-eight cents versus eighty-seven cents expected — as gross margins fell two hundred and thirty basis points year-over-year to twelve point four percent. Management's commentary was cautious, calling out stubborn interest rates, high fuel costs, and inflation squeezing household budgets. North American towable RV backlog did surge roughly seventy-five percent year-over-year, but motorized RV backlog fell twenty-eight percent. No formal guidance until later this fall.

Finally, Pentair named a new CFO, Bob Hau, effective November first. He brings experience from Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox. Routine leadership transition, nothing alarming.

Bottom line for today: Viking is the momentum story, AutoZone is a low-quality beat that could face selling pressure, and THOR is a macro warning flag on the consumer. Stay focused and size accordingly.
